newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HK's Wah Tak Fung sees steady earnings growth.
newsitem.headline: HK's Wah Tak Fung sees steady earnings growth.

text.p: Office property developer and investor Wah Tak Fung Holdings Ltd sees steady earnings growth in coming years, the company said on Monday.

"A limited supply of Grade B office in Hong Kong and an increasing demand from tenants and buyers from China-related companies in wake of relaxation of China economic control are seen as creating demand for the Grade B office," the company's executive director David Chu told a news conference.
As property prices for Grade B offices fluctuated less than Grade A offices, a recent recovery in Grade A would mean a boost in Grade B later, the company's managing director Richard Chan said.
"Our strategy will continue to be developing office buildings in non-office buildings areas," Chan added.
Offices in Hong Kong are normally graded in A, B, and C.

The company's director Kennneth Chan said office property accounted for 84 percent of its property portfolio and 16 percent was from residential property which the company used for rental income purposes.
Among office property, 75 percent are for sale and 25 for rental purposes, Chan added.
Wah Tak Fung has a land bank of 44,700 sq. metres, including six properties for investment, three under development, one under turnkey development, three held for sale and one for future development.
The properties were valued at HK$2.565 billion as at June 30, 1996.

The company posted a profit of HK$62.32 million for the year ended March 31, 1996, up from HK$57.18 million in 1995 and HK$56.19 million in 1994. It forecast its profits to increase to HK$80 million for the year ending 1997.

Wah Tak Fung plans to issue 138 million new shares, or 25 percent of the expanded share capital, at HK$1.88 per share, raising net proceeds of HK$245 million to fund its development projects and for working capital.
The company's financial controller Shirley Hui said the company's gearing ratio would be reduced to 73 percent following the new issue from 104 percent.
